model: Insurer distributable operating earnings (FCFE) capitalised at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management 2025-28 operating EPS CAGR target (11% from a 55p 2025 baseline), corroborated by the 12% operating EPS CAGR 2022-25 (39.9p -> 56.0p); not the equity CAGR, which is broken by the IFRS 17 restatement, the 2022 GBP3.75bn capital return and the CSM sitting outside IFRS equity.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: IFRS series are not on one basis: revenue (total income) 3yr +13.9% includes Direct Line from Jul-2025 and the IFRS 17 regime; 5yr revenue -10.4%, basic EPS -17.5% and equity -13.1% reflect the 2021 disposals (FY2020 net income GBP2,798m was disposal-inflated), the 2022 IFRS 17 restatement and the 2022 consolidation/capital return. Equity CAGR diverges >30pp from the operating EPS CAGR; the operating EPS and DPS series are the only comparable ones.
historical_growth.notes: eps_3yr_cagr and fcf_3yr_cagr are the operating EPS CAGR 2022-25 (FY2025 results presentation); basic IFRS EPS FY2022 was negative (-34.7p, IFRS 17 transition) so no 3yr CAGR exists on that line. DPS 31.0p (FY2022) -> 39.3p (FY2025) = 8.2%/yr; FY2025 included a one-off 5% uplift for Direct Line. Shareholders' equity 9,408 (FY2022) -> 9,694 (FY2025) after GBP2.9bn of dividends and GBP0.6bn of buybacks; H1 2026 equity 8,910 on 3,002m shares = 297p BVPS, i.e. the price is ~2.3x book, which is why a P/B model was not used.

scenario_narratives.base: Direct Line integration delivers as guided: GBP225m cost synergies by 2028 and >GBP500m capital synergies lift the Solvency II ratio into the high-180s by end-2026, restoring the GBP300-400m annual buyback cadence on top of a dividend growing mid-single digits. UK&I GI holds COR below 94% as rate keeps pace with motor repair inflation; Canada reaches ~94%. Wealth compounds on net flows and the Pensions Schemes Bill toward the GBP280m 2027 ambition; Retirement grows modestly as individual annuities and equity release offset BPA volumes ceded on pricing discipline. Operating EPS compounds ~11% to 2028 (75p) then growth fades toward nominal GDP as synergies lapse. About 88% of attributable operating profit is distributable each year.
scenario_narratives.bull: Synergies run ahead (as the November 2025 upgrade from GBP125m to GBP225m already did), capital synergies exceed GBP500m and the solvency ratio sits comfortably above the 160-180% working range, so buybacks step up toward GBP500m+ and the payout rises to ~90%. Motor claims inflation normalises after the 2024-25 spike, letting the enlarged personal-lines book earn a low-90s COR; UK commercial pricing stabilises; BPA pricing rationalises and Aviva re-enters at scale at its low-teens IRR hurdle; Wealth beats GBP280m. Operating profit grows ~20% in 2026 and high single digits through 2029, fading to 3%, and the market pays a mature-compounder 14x on the exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: Motor repair inflation (claims costs +23% in 2025, ~39% above 2023) outruns rate, Irish and Canadian weather losses recur, and the enlarged personal-lines book earns a mid-90s COR rather than a low-90s one; integration slips and the PRA is slow to approve the internal-model consolidation, so capital synergies and the solvency rebuild arrive late and buybacks are deferred (as they were in FY2025). Commercial lines keep shrinking and BPA share continues to go to L&G, so Retirement stalls. Operating profit still rises ~13% in 2026 on the Direct Line consolidation (H1 is already reported at +24%) but then stagnates at ~2% a year, more capital is retained (16% of pre-tax profit), the tax rate drifts to 25%, and the exit multiple compresses to 12x FCFE.
scenario_narratives.capex_pct_meaning: In every scenario capex_pct_path is NOT capital expenditure: it is the share of pre-tax Group adjusted operating profit that does not reach ordinary shareholders (NCI, Tier 1 coupons, capital retained for new-business strain and Solvency II buffers).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Aviva is valued as the stream of operating earnings it can actually hand to ordinary shareholders - Group adjusted operating profit after tax, NCI, Tier 1 coupons and the capital it must retain to write new business and hold its Solvency II buffer - capitalised at a GBP cost of equity of 10.5%, with no net-debt deduction because the subordinated debt is already serviced inside the flow. The three scenarios differ on the Direct Line synergy path, the general-insurance combined ratio against motor claims inflation and weather, the BPA/commercial-lines discipline that caps growth, and how much of the profit the solvency position allows out of the door. Book value is deliberately not the anchor: the CSM carries GBP7-8bn of recognised-but-unearned profit outside IFRS equity and the series was broken by IFRS 17 and the 2022 capital return. The result is a high-single-digit-yield compounder: at the current price the market pays ~10.9x FY2026 operating EPS for a 5.8% dividend yield plus buybacks.
key_risks_to_valuation: Direct Line integration: GBP225m cost synergies and >GBP500m capital synergies depend on systems migration and PRA approval of the internal-model consolidation; a delay pushes the solvency rebuild and buybacks right

Motor claims and repair inflation (+23% in 2025) and weather/catastrophe losses in Ireland and Canada against the <94% UK&I COR target; each 1pp of COR on ~GBP14bn of GI premiums is ~GBP140m of pre-tax profit

Solvency II sensitivity: 176% at H1 2026 inside a 160-180% working range; equity, credit-spread and rate shocks or model changes can defer capital returns, which this model assumes resume at GBP300-400m a year
Growth ceded on pricing discipline: BPA PVNBP -44% and UK commercial GWP -6-8% - if the market does not rationalise, the post-2028 fade arrives sooner
Cost of equity: every 1pp on a 10.5% CoE moves the base value roughly 12-14% in the opposite direction; the required_return_table shows the implied return at the current price
Model definition risk: 'distributable' is a judgment (12.5% retention in base); if Aviva retains more to fund BPA or M&A, FCFE is lower even with the same operating profit

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 590.6-740.6 GBp
data_sources.financials: AV.L_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (HY26 results pack, 14 Aug 2026: notes B1/B2 operating profit and operating EPS reconciliation, E12 share counts and dilution, C1 cash remittances, D Solvency II); AV.L_Annual_FY2025.txt (FY2025 annual report, 5 Mar 2026); AV.L_Metrics.csv / core_metrics for the history; AV.L_Presentation_H1-2026.txt for the 2025-28 targets and the 2026 outlook
data_sources.qualitative: AV.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-05): business model, Direct Line integration, guidance table, bull/bear points

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2025 Group adjusted operating profit before tax (GBP m), the flow the engine's 'revenue' line carries. It is stated AFTER corporate centre costs and external debt interest, BEFORE operating tax, non-controlling interests and Tier 1 note coupons. Direct Line is consolidated from 1 July 2025, so FY2025 holds only half a year of it.
inputs.share_count_basis: 3,002m shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (HY26 note E12(a)(iii)) plus 31m dilutive share awards and options (note E12(b)) = 3,033m fully diluted. Held FLAT: distributable earnings (which fund dividends AND buybacks) are deducted as FCFE, so a shrinking count on top would double-count the buyback. The GBP350m buyback was essentially complete at 30 June (56m shares) and finished in July 2026.
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at ZERO by construction. Aviva's Group adjusted operating profit is already after 'Group debt costs and other interest' (~GBP300m/yr), so the subordinated debt (GBP6,057m borrowings at 30 June 2026, Solvency II leverage 30.8%) is serviced inside the flow and capitalising that flow at the cost of equity values the equity directly; deducting the debt again would charge it twice. The GBP21.2bn cash is dominated by policyholder funds and is not shareholder surplus. Tier 1 note coupons and NCI are charged via the retention line (capex_pct_path).
inputs.fcf_definition: FY2025 distributable operating earnings on the model's definition: 2,203 x (1 - 24% operating tax - 12.5% NCI/Tier-1/capital retention) = GBP1,399m. The IFRS cash-flow statement (OCF -2,563 FY2025, +4,485 H1 2026) is policyholder-flow noise and is not used. Cross-check: FY2025 attributable operating profit GBP1,600m (56.0p x 2,855m); cash returned on the FY2025 result = GBP1,034m dividends paid in-year + GBP350m buyback launched March 2026 = GBP1,384m.
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based payments are expensed inside Group adjusted operating profit under IFRS 2 and never added back; dilution from awards is in the 31m dilutive count. No separate SBC charge, so house and street bases coincide (band collapses).
inputs.buyback_note: GBP347m repurchased in H1 2026 (GBP350m programme launched 5 March 2026, completed July 2026). FY2025 buyback cash was nil (capital reserved for Direct Line); FY2022-24 GBP300-336m per year. Buybacks are value-neutral here: they are one of the two mechanisms by which the modelled FCFE reaches shareholders.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp, 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP/share to quote pence/share; a fixed identity, no market rate or parity check required.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T15:35:18Z regular LSE close (Friday); no Monday 2026-10-05 print available from Yahoo at build time
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in GBP, the flows' own currency: UK 10-year gilt ~4.6% + beta ~1.1 (composite insurer with annuity credit and GI catastrophe exposure) x 5.5% ERP = ~10.6%, rounded to 10.5%. Used in all three scenarios so that risk is charged once, through the scenario weights, not again through per-scenario discount rates. Sell-side UK life/composite CoE assumptions cluster at 9-11%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease costs (IFRS 16 depreciation and interest, lease liabilities GBP450m) sit inside operating profit; no separate lease charge and no lease liability in the bridge (net debt is zero on this route).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests (GBP21m FY2025, GBP9m H1 2026) and Tier 1 note coupons (GBP63m FY2025, GBP37m H1 2026, higher after the GBP500m RT1 issued March 2025 and the GBP350m RT1 acquired with Direct Line) are deducted from after-tax operating profit through the retention line, so the modelled FCFE is attributable to ordinary shareholders only.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE-at-cost-of-equity for a composite insurer, run through the owner-FCF engine with the drivers re-purposed: 'revenue' = Group adjusted operating profit before tax; ebitda_margin 100%; sbc, lease, D&A and working capital zero; cash_tax_rate = operating effective tax rate (24%, HY26 note B2); capex_pct_path = the share of pre-tax operating profit that does NOT reach ordinary shareholders (NCI + Tier 1 coupons ~3.6pp, plus capital retained to fund new-business strain and Solvency II buffer growth ~9pp in base) so FCF = distributable operating earnings; net_debt 0 because the flow is post-interest; WACC = cost of equity. ROUTING: SKILL.md sends insurers to BVPS-compounding x exit P/B, but Aviva trades at ~2.1x IFRS book (317p BVPS at FY2025, 297p at H1 2026) and is managed, guided and priced on operating EPS (11% CAGR 2025-28), Solvency II own-funds generation (OCG ~20pts p.a. from 2027) and cash remittances (>GBP7bn 2026-28); book value is a poor anchor because IFRS 17 equity excludes the CSM (GBP7-8bn of future profit) and the 2022 restatement broke the series. Capitalising distributable operating earnings at CoE is the same discipline the REIT/AFFO builds use and reconciles to the dividend + buyback cash the company actually returns. CROSS-CHECKS: FY2025 model FCFE GBP1,399m vs cash returned GBP1,384m; FY2026 model FCFE ~GBP1,650m vs guided dividend cash cost ~GBP1.27bn + a buyback of the FY2026 size (GBP350m) = ~GBP1.62bn; FY2026 implied pre-tax operating profit GBP2,600m vs H1 actual GBP1,326m (H1 was 48% of the FY in 2025) and vs 11% operating EPS growth on 56.0p = 62.2p x ~3,020m weighted shares = GBP1,880m attributable = GBP2,600m pre-tax at 24% tax after NCI/T1. GUIDANCE ANCHORS (HY26, 14 Aug 2026): FY2026 operating EPS growth broadly in line with the 11% target; UK&I GI COR <94% (89.5% undiscounted at H1); Canada COR approaching 94%; Solvency II cover ratio high-180s by end-2026 (176% at 30 June) after >GBP350m of Direct Line capital synergies; mid-single-digit growth in the dividend cash cost; Direct Line cost synergies GBP225m run-rate by 2028 (c.GBP130m by end-2026). DATA CAVEATS: IFRS 4 -> IFRS 17 at FY2023 (FY2022 restated); 2021 continuing-only after the disposals; 76-for-100 consolidation in 2022; Direct Line step-up from 1 July 2025 - none of the IFRS revenue, net income, EPS or equity CAGRs are on one basis, which is why historical_growth is anchored on operating EPS and DPS only. PRICE: Friday 2 Oct 2026 regular close; refresh at the next close.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +18% to GBP2,600m: full-year Direct Line (H1 +24% reported), c.GBP130m cumulative cost synergies, COR inside target; equals ~11% operating EPS growth after the share-count step-up. FY2027-28 +9%/+7.5% delivers the 11% EPS CAGR to 2028 (75p) once ~1.5-2%/yr of buyback accretion is stripped out, carried by the remaining GBP95m of cost synergies, Wealth to GBP280m, UK GI rate adequacy and Canada COR. Fade to 2.5% nominal by year 9 as the synergy tailwind ends and BPA/commercial-lines discipline caps volume.
base.capex_rationale: Retention line, % of pre-tax operating profit: NCI + Tier 1 coupons ~3.6pp (GBP95m on GBP2.6bn) plus ~9pp of after-tax profit retained for new-business strain and Solvency II buffer growth. Leaves ~88% of attributable operating profit distributable, matching FY2024 actual (GBP1,221m returned on GBP1,290m attributable = 95%) and FY2025 (GBP1,384m incl. the March-2026 buyback on GBP1,600m = 87%), and consistent with OCG of ~20pts of the GBP8.9bn SCR (~GBP1.8bn) from 2027 against ~GBP1.65bn of dividends and buybacks.
base.tax_rationale: Operating effective tax rate 24% in FY2025 and H1 2026 (UK 25% statutory blended with Canada ~26% and Ireland 12.5%); no NOL or one-off in the base.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 10.5%/2.5% = 12.8x year-10 FCFE, so the 13x cap does not bind in base; 12.8x FCFE on an ~88% payout is ~11.3x operating earnings, in line with where UK composites trade through the cycle.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because two of its drivers are live, not hypothetical: motor claims inflation has run 13% and 23% in consecutive years, and the capital-synergy case rests on a PRA approval that has not yet been granted, at a company previously fined for a Solvency II internal-model error. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs synergies, claims inflation, BPA pricing and Wealth all to break the right way at once, and the muted reaction to a strong H1 2026 suggests the market already credits delivery. Base at 50%: three-year targets were set in March 2026 off an H1 that is tracking them.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
